root.name: Tarrasch Defense: Symmetrical Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. e3 Nf6 5. Nf3 Nc6

overview: Both sides have mirrored pawns on c, d and e files and develop knights. White chooses between 6.a3, 6.Bd3 and 6.dxc5 and Black replies ...cxd4 exd4 to reach a symmetrical IQP position or ...a6 and ...dxc4 for a flexible game. The structure is balanced and about manoeuvring, with an eventual IQP or hanging pawns.

white_ideas.idea: Play a3 and dxc5 or Bd3 to seek a small edge, with cxd5 to change the structure.
Aim at an IQP structure where White blockades or presses with pieces.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...cxd4 exd4 and ...Be7 for an IQP position with active pieces.
Or ...a6 and ...dxc4 Bxc4 b5 to gain queenside space.

typical_structures.structure: Hanging pawns on c5 and d5 if both sides recapture accordingly.

character.notes: Slow, manoeuvring play with a symmetrical structure and long-term weaknesses; not forcing.

structure.notes: Symmetric exchange structure with one open file after cxd4 exd4; undecided until then.

approach.notes: A mainstream Semi-Tarrasch/Tarrasch move order, played by strong players.

level.notes: IQP and hanging-pawn play need judgement more than memory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.dxc5
sublines_that_differ.how: Leads to hanging pawns on c4/d4 rather than an IQP.

character.reason: Symmetrical, manoeuvring, and not especially safe or forcing.

structure.reason: Symmetrical exchange structure with an open file; tension until resolved.

plans.reason: IQP or hanging pawns in a symmetrical set-up.
